title: The back-and-forth relation of the linear order transfers to the labelled tree at a shift of two
source_title: Scott sentence complexities of linear orderings

standard_prerequisites.name: The linear order attached to a structure
standard_prerequisites.statement: A structure A carries a linear order L_A of labelled blocks, and the labelled tree T_A of its finite tuples is coded inside it.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the pair of objects the lemma relates.

standard_prerequisites.name: The coding map f
standard_prerequisites.statement: The map f sends the elements of L_A to the corresponding nodes of the labelled tree, so that comparing f applied to a tuple compares the coded tuples.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the map through which the two relations are compared.

standard_prerequisites.name: Back-and-forth relations of both structures
standard_prerequisites.statement: The rank alpha back-and-forth relations are defined by the game of that rank, and a rank comparison is decided by the interval relations left after each move.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the two relations shown to correspond at shifted ranks.

core_obligations: Prove the statement by transfinite induction and isolate the base case, which is the only interesting one (source lines 622-625).

For the easy direction note that the label and predecessor relations of the tree are definable in the order at rank three, so a formula of rank one about the coded tuple translates into a formula of rank three about the tuple, giving the forward implication (source lines 625-628).

For the converse assume the coded comparison and run the game: after the opponent plays a tuple, answer with elements that have the same label and the same position in their block and that restore the tree isomorphism, which the coded comparison guarantees exist (source lines 630-638).

On the last turn answer so that the intervals between the chosen elements are at least as large as those on the other side, which is possible because between any two elements in different blocks there are blocks coding paths of arbitrarily large size (source lines 638-644).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the induction to the base case.
Forward direction from the definability of label and predecessor at rank three.
Converse: answer with same-label, same-position elements.
Last turn: match the interval sizes using the replicated path blocks.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source0.tex lines 616-620: for a tuple whose elements from labelled blocks are accompanied by their whole blocks, the tuple stands in the rank three plus alpha relation to another such tuple exactly when the coded tuples stand in the rank one plus alpha relation in the labelled tree. The statement is a rank bookkeeping assertion, and the proof (source lines 621-645) has to earn it from both sides: the forward implication rests on the label and predecessor relations of the tree being definable in the order at rank three, while the converse is a two-turn strategy in the back-and-forth game in which the existential player first has to find elements with the same label and the same position inside their block that restore the tree isomorphism, and then has to match the sizes of all intervals at once, which uses that between two elements in different blocks there are blocks coding paths of arbitrarily large size. Neither the definability shift nor the interval-matching argument is visible in the statement.
